reasoning_note: FTP from clinical subnet at 2am looks odd but could easily be a scheduled legacy backup job nobody documented.
47 records from a billing user is a slow Tuesday night, probably month-end reconciliation or audit prep.
Cross-VLAN SMB from admin to medical device is unusual but could be an IT tech pushing a firmware update during the day.
340 MB SFTP out from the lab server is suspicious but labs routinely send results to reference lab partners, need to check if dest is whitelisted.
Infusion pump hitting an external HTTPS endpoint at 6am is almost certainly a vendor cloud check-in or update poll.
High-volume DNS from a medical device to internal DNS is normal chatter, these things are noisy by design.
Float nurse covering multiple departments at 2:30am accessing 31 records is completely plausible during a night shift.
ICMP sweep from the management VLAN at 10am is almost certainly a network monitoring tool doing its job.
RDP from admin to device subnet on a Saturday morning looks like scheduled maintenance, probably a tech doing weekend patching.
4.8 GB PACS transfer out could be a teleradiology feed but the volume is large enough to warrant confirming the destination is a known partner.
Another large PACS outbound transfer at 4am, probably the same scheduled replication or teleradiology job as A-14.
Proprietary wireless to an unknown device is vague enough to be a Bluetooth peripheral pairing but the 8.0 severity and lack of detail means I should at least look.
312 records in 8 minutes from a service account at 1am could be a scheduled report but the speed and breadth across all departments is worth verifying the job exists.
Telnet from a ventilator is genuinely weird since no modern clinical workflow should use telnet, but I want to confirm it is not a misconfigured management agent before escalating.
EHR to backup server over SMB at 14:30 is textbook scheduled backup, 28 GB is a normal full DB dump size.
890 MB HTTPS out from pharmacy on a Saturday night is likely an automated inventory sync with a wholesaler or cloud PMS.
Patient monitor sending 5x traffic to its own VLAN gateway at 3am could be a firmware update download or a sensor glitch, not alarming.
The EHR server itself port-scanning the entire internal network at 3am is not a false positive pattern I have ever seen, this box may be compromised.
Physician accessing 22 records via VPN at 9:45pm is a doctor doing evening chart reviews from home, completely normal.
1.1 GB exfiltrated from a nurse station in 3 minutes to an Eastern European IP block during business hours is the one alert today that actually looks like data theft.

q21_note: These alerts are pure network metadata with no patient identifiers or clinical context, a nurse would have no idea what any of this means for patient safety.
q22_note: The network details support triage decisions but without asset inventory confirmation and destination reputation lookups, management would still ask me to go verify before approving any action.
